newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Eastern says metal price hits profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Eastern says metal price hits profit.

text.p: Eastern Aluminium Ltd, which holds 10 percent of Australia's Portland smelter, said on Thursday a weak aluminium price and a strong Australian dollar weighed unfavourably on its bottom line in 1996.
Eastern earlier on Wednesday reported a 56 percent drop in net profit to A$4.64 million for calendar 1996.
"Average aluminium prices received in 1996 were 17.8 percent lower and the average Australian dollar to U.S. dollar exchange rate received was 6.1 percent higher than in 1995," Eastern said.
The company's share of aluminium production at Portland in 1996 was 29,182 tonnes, which was marginally higher than 1995 production share of 29,043 tonnes.

As a consequence of new metal sales arrangements introduced in 1996, the company now carries modest operating stocks. As a result, 1996 sales of 28,567 tonnes were slightly lower than in 1995 when all production was sold, Eastern said.
The company's main operating costs are for alumina and power, both of which flex with aluminium prices with a lag of three months, it said.
The demand outlook for aluminium is strong, particularly in Asia, the company said.

"The industry is continuing to adjust to the over-supply position of the early 1990s. Aluminium prices have recovered from the low levels of the second half of 1996 and the current price of around $US 1,575/tonne is well ahead of the average 1996 price of $US1,506/tonne," Eastern said.
If prices can be maintained at around current levels, profits will improve through 1997, the company said.
Market premiums that the company earns on aluminium sales will also be higher in 1997, it said.

With the recent weakening of the Australian dollar-U.S. dollar exchange rate, the current aluminium price in Australian dollar terms is around A$2,050/tonne compared with an average of $1,820/tonne in the second half of 1996, Eastern noted.
Portland is owned 45 percent by Alcoa of Australia Ltd , 25 percent by the Victorian state government and 10 percent each by Eastern, Marubeni Corp and China International Trust and Investment Corp.
